title: wish, if only, would rather, it's time
tagline: Five ways to say things aren't the way you want them — each with its own tense.
exam: Reading & Use of English Part 4 — key word transformations
Reading & Use of English Part 2 — open cloze (wish / rather / as / though)
Speaking Part 2 — expressing preference and regret about a photo or situation
why: Wishing, regretting and preferring all sound similar in Spanish but need very different English tenses. B2 First tests whether you know that wish looks backwards with the past, that would rather changes tense when it's about someone else, and that as if can make an ordinary sentence sound doubtful just by choosing the past.

diagrams.title: wish + past, past perfect or would?

rows.label: Time reference
cells: the future / a change in behaviour

rows.label: Example
cells: I wish I had more free time.
I wish I had studied harder.
I wish you would stop interrupting.

branches.label: wish / if only + past simple
items: I wish I lived nearer the beach.

branches.label: wish / if only + past perfect
items: I wish I hadn't said that.
If only we had left earlier.

branches.label: wish / if only + would
items: I wish he would text back.
If only it would stop raining.

branches.label: would rather + past simple
items: I'd rather you told me the truth.
I'd rather we didn't argue about this.

branches.label: it's (high) time + past simple
items: It's high time this rule changed.

diagrams.title: as if / as though — sounding doubtful

parts.ex: talks as if he owned the place
looked as if she had seen a ghost

diagrams.caption: The past tense after as if / as though signals that the comparison probably isn't true.

formula.chip: regret or a wish for change

head: Structure
Pattern
Example
Meaning
rows: I wish I had a louder alarm clock.
I wish I hadn't skipped breakfast.
I wish Liam would tidy his desk.
I'd rather you didn't tell her yet.
a preference about another person's action
It's time we left for the station.
She acts as if she knew everything.
a comparison that is probably untrue

use.point: wish / if only + past simple: a regret about the present

examples.text: I wish I had more time to practise before the audition.
examples.note: a present situation you'd like to be different

examples.text: If only the wifi were faster during the exam week.
examples.note: were, not was, in careful written English

use.point: wish / if only + past perfect: a regret about the past

examples.text: Sofia wishes she hadn't deleted her project files the night before.
examples.note: a specific past action she regrets

examples.text: If only we had checked the schedule before booking the flights.
I wish I had listened to Miss Vega's advice about the essay structure.

use.point: wish / if only + would: irritation with someone else's behaviour, or a wish for change

examples.text: I wish Liam would stop checking his phone during rehearsals.
If only the buses would run on time in the mornings.
examples.note: a wish about something outside your control

examples.text: I wish the neighbours would turn the music down; it's midnight.
examples.note: irritation, not a fact about now

use.point: would rather and it's time: preferences and things that should already be happening

examples.text: I'd rather you asked me before borrowing my notes next time.
examples.note: would rather + past simple for another person's action

examples.text: It's time the school updated its recycling policy.
examples.note: it's time + past simple, present meaning

examples.text: Mateo talks about the final as if he'd already won it.
examples.note: as if + past perfect for a doubtful comparison

watch_out.wrong: I wish I would be taller.
watch_out.why: For a wish about your own present state, use the past simple, not would.

watch_out.wrong: I wish I would have studied harder for the test.
watch_out.right: I wish I had studied harder for the test.
watch_out.why: A regret about a finished past action needs the past perfect, not would have.

watch_out.wrong: I wish I would remember everyone's name.
watch_out.why: Wish + would is for someone else's behaviour, not your own ability — use wish + could instead.

watch_out.wrong: I'd rather you don't mention it to her.
watch_out.right: I'd rather you didn't mention it to her.
watch_out.why: After would rather + someone else, use the past simple, even though the meaning is present or future.

watch_out.wrong: It's time we leave for the airport.
watch_out.right: It's time we left for the airport.
watch_out.why: It's (high) time takes the past simple, with a present meaning: this should be happening now.

watch_out.wrong: He talks as if he is an expert on everything.
watch_out.right: He talks as if he were an expert on everything.
watch_out.why: When the comparison is probably untrue, as if / as though take a past form, even for the present.

dialogue.title: The group project deadline
dialogue.context: Sofia, Liam and Nadia are finishing a group project the night before it's due, in the school library in Lima.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: I wish we had started this last week instead of leaving it until now.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: Same. If only Mateo hadn't cancelled the meeting on Tuesday, we'd be finished.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Honestly, I wish you two would stop blaming each other and just type.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Fair. It's time we focused and finished the last section.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: I'd rather you checked my paragraph before I send it — my grammar's a bit shaky tonight.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Sure. Also, I wish the library would extend its hours during deadline week.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Tell me about it. Miss Vega acts as if deadlines were never a problem for her students.

lines.speaker: Liam
lines.text: That's because she plans everything early. I wish I were that organised.

lines.speaker: Nadia
lines.text: Well, next term, maybe. For now, if only this printer would work — it's jammed again.

lines.speaker: Sofia
lines.text: Of course it is. I wish something around here went right just once tonight.

items.sentence: I wish I ___ more confident before presentations.
items.why: a present state you'd like different → wish + past simple

items.sentence: If only she ___ her notes before the exam started.
items.why: a regret about a finished past action → wish + past perfect

items.sentence: I wish my brother ___ borrowing my things without asking.
items.why: irritation at someone else's repeated behaviour → wish + would

items.sentence: I'd rather you ___ me before changing the plan next time.
items.why: would rather + another person's action → past simple

items.sentence: It's high time the team ___ a new strategy.
items.why: it's (high) time + past simple, present meaning

items.sentence: Nadia speaks Italian as if she ___ there for years.
items.why: a doubtful comparison further back → as if + past perfect

items.second_end: leaving his bag in the doorway.

items.first: Please don't post that photo — I'd prefer it.
We should have left for the station five minutes ago.
He speaks about the trip as though it's already been booked, but it hasn't.

summary: wish / if only + past simple = a regret about now; + past perfect = a regret about the past; + would = irritation at someone or something else.
Wish + would almost never takes I as its subject — it's for other people's behaviour, not your own.
Would rather + another person's action uses the past simple, even with a present or future meaning.
It's (high) time + past simple says something should already be happening.
As if / as though + a past form makes a comparison sound doubtful, even when it describes the present.
